records_to_check.source:
The year is 1518 - a year before Hernán Cortes would be elected captain of the third expedition to the South American mainland, where he would overthrow the Aztec empire. But that will not happen, because you have beaten him to the punch.

You are the eldest child of a Spanish nobleman, and you yourself hold the title of Hidalgo. With your father's backing, you have been the leader of a successful "hermandad" (meaning "brotherhood") back in the Old World - a peacekeeping association of armed individuals which protected the countryside around your father's town.

During this time, you demonstrated an aptitude for leadership and strategy that earned you the respect of the people under your command - but it was time for a greater challenge. With the King's permission and your father's financial support, you purchased a ship and selected your crew from the best of the brothers and sisters in your hermandad.

Together, you are off on the long and arduous journey to explore the New World. In your cargo hold, you bring rations, medicine, equipment, and assorted valuables. You must first make a stop on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, under Spanish domain since 1496. Here, you will hire servants or buy slaves, rest and restock, and gain what information you can about the New World.

After five weeks on the Atlantic Ocean, your people gather on the deck as the call "Land ahoy!" rings out from the rigging. On a clear afternoon, gulls screeching in the wake of your ship, you sail into the port of Santo Domingo, the seat of Spanish colonial rule in the New World.
records_to_check.translation:
现在是 1518 年——再过一年，埃尔南·科尔特斯就会当选第三支远征队的队长，前往南美洲大陆，并推翻阿兹特克帝国。但这一切不会发生，因为你抢在了他前头。

你是西班牙一位贵族最年长的孩子，自己也拥有伊达尔戈头衔。在父亲的支持下，你曾在旧大陆成功领导一个名为“hermandad”（意为“兄弟会”）的组织——这是一个由武装人员组成的治安团体，负责保护你父亲所在城镇周边的乡间地区。

在此期间，你展现出卓越的领导力与战略眼光，赢得了麾下众人的敬重——但如今，该迎接更大的挑战了。在国王许可和父亲资助下，你买下一艘船只，并从兄弟会的成员中挑选出最优秀的男女，组成船员队伍。

你们就此踏上漫长而艰辛的旅程，去探索新大陆。货舱里装着口粮、药品、装备以及各种贵重物品。你们必须先在加勒比海的伊斯帕尼奥拉岛停靠；自 1496 年起，该岛便处于西班牙的统治之下。在那里，你们会雇用仆人或购买奴隶，休整并补充物资，还要尽可能打听新大陆的消息。

横渡大西洋五周后，桅杆上响起“陆地！陆地！”的呼喊，你的同伴们纷纷聚集到甲板上。一个晴朗的午后，海鸥在船尾啼叫，你们驶入圣多明各港口——这里是西班牙在新大陆殖民统治的中心。

在此期间，你展现出卓越的领导力与战略眼光，赢得了麾下众人的敬重——但如今，该迎接更大的挑战了。在国王许可和父亲资助下，你买下一艘船只，并从兄弟会的成员中挑选出最优秀的男女，组成船员队伍。

横渡大西洋五周后，桅杆上响起“陆地！陆地！”的呼喊，你的同伴们纷纷聚集到甲板上。一个晴朗的午后，海鸥在船尾啼叫，你们驶入圣多明各港口——这里是西班牙在新大陆殖民统治的中心。

records_to_check.source:
The year is 1518 - a year before Hernán Cortes would be elected captain of the third expedition to the South American mainland, where he would overthrow the Aztec empire. But that will not happen, because you have beaten him to the punch.

You are the eldest child of a Spanish nobleman, and you yourself hold the title of Hidalgo. With your father's backing, you have been the leader of a successful "hermandad" (meaning "brotherhood") back in the Old World - a peacekeeping association of armed individuals which protected the countryside around your father's town.

During this time, you demonstrated an aptitude for leadership and strategy that earned you the respect of the people under your command - but it was time for a greater challenge. With the King's permission and your father's financial support, you purchased a ship and selected your crew from the best of the brothers and sisters in your hermandad.

Together, you are off on the long and arduous journey to explore the New World. In your cargo hold, you bring rations, medicine, equipment, and assorted valuables. You must first make a stop on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, under Spanish domain since 1496. Here, you will hire servants or buy slaves, rest and restock, and gain what information you can about the New World.

After five weeks on the Atlantic Ocean, your people gather on the deck as the call "Land ahoy!" rings out from the rigging. On a clear afternoon, gulls screeching in the wake of your ship, you sail into the port of Santo Domingo, the seat of Spanish colonial rule in the New World.

records_to_check.source: Born in 1469, he had a relatively normal childhood, growing up in a small farm town. He met the love of his life, whom he married at a young age. He was apprenticing as an alchemist when his wife fell ill from typhus and died a short while later. The loss sent him into a deep depression and he buried himself in his work and the field of disease treatment. He never fully recovered from his broken heart, and partly the reason he joined your expedition was to get over his grief. A somber and quiet man, but no man knows better the field of diseases and infections than he.
records_to_check.translation: 他生于1469年，童年生活相当平凡，在一座小型农庄镇长大。他很早便与一生挚爱结了婚。当他还在做炼金术士学徒时，妻子染上斑疹伤寒，不久便去世了。这场失去让他陷入深深的抑郁；他把自己埋进工作中，专心钻研疾病治疗。他始终没能从心碎中完全恢复，而他加入你们的远征，部分原因也是想走出悲痛。他是个沉郁寡言的人，但论疾病与感染，无人比他更精通。

records_to_check.source: The Hungarian mercenary is a powerfully built man who looks particularly imposing in his black piecemeal armour. He was trained in Hungary's Black Army and fought against the Turks as well as a peasant rebellion. After the dissolution of the Fekete sereg, his company struck out on their own and he travelled to Italy to fight as a mercenary. Now he has come to the New World searching for his old friend, Tamás Szász.

records_to_check.source: Perhaps sensing that your debate is getting to Esteban, FNameFirst1 draws a knife from FHisHer1 boot and plunges it as deep into the huge man's chest as it will go. Esteban howls out in pain and momentarily releases his hold on FNameFirst1, but just as FHeShe1 writhes out of the giant's reach, Esteban's sword comes slashing down and tears right through FHisHer1 uniform, painting an arc of blood across the ground. Without a sound, FNameFirst1 collapses on the ground, and for the briefest of moments, all seems silent. Then all hell breaks loose as your people raise their weapons and hurl themselves at Esteban's tribal allies.
records_to_check.translation: 也许是看出你的争论让埃斯特班动摇了，FNameFirst1从FHisHer1靴子里抽出一把小刀，尽可能深地刺进那个大汉的胸膛。埃斯特班痛苦地嚎叫，暂时松开了抓住FNameFirst1的手；可就在FHeShe1挣脱巨人的控制时，埃斯特班的剑猛然劈下，划破了FHisHer1制服，血迹在地上划出一道弧线。FNameFirst1一声不响地倒在地上，短短一瞬间，四周仿佛一片寂静。随后，地狱般的混战骤然爆发，你的人举起武器，冲向埃斯特班的部族盟友。

records_to_check.source: The daughter of Andres de Yruenes, who was a part of Columbus' crew. Isabela's mother was a Taíno woman, and as a child of two worlds, Isabela has never found it easy to fit in. Despite her difficulties in gaining the trust of her mother's tribesmen, and the often terrible treatment she sustained from the colonists in Santo Domingo, Isabela has stubbornly held on to a positive outlook on life. She is far from naive, having seen many of the worst sides of people, but she is a stoically polite and open-minded woman who fights for peace and reconciliation for both her peoples.
records_to_check.translation: 哥伦布船员之一安德烈斯·德·尤鲁埃内斯之女。伊莎贝拉的母亲是一位泰诺人。作为两个世界的孩子，伊莎贝拉始终难以融入其中。尽管她难以取得母亲族人的信任，也常遭圣多明各殖民者恶劣对待，她仍顽强地保持着乐观的人生态度。她绝非天真无知，早已见识过人性最恶劣的一面；但她是一位沉着、礼貌、思想开放的女性，为两个族群的和平与和解而奋斗。

"Un sobrynn' est' abadessa avi', a que mui gran ben 
queria, que era men' e apost' e fremoso. 
Este, des que viu a monja, quis-lle mellor d'outra ren, 
e en guisar que a ouvesse foi tan aguçoso, que non era dia 
que ll' el muitas vegadas sa coita non dizia e lle prometia 
que sse con el sse fosse, con ela casaria."
records_to_check.translation:
“修女院长有个侄儿，她很疼爱他；
他年轻、端庄又俊美。
他一见那修女，便觉得她胜过世间一切；
为了得到她，他费尽心思，十分急切，
日日多次向她倾诉自己的苦恋，还许诺说：
只要她跟他走，他就娶她为妻。”

The first African slaves landed on Hispaniola in 1501, and were destined for the mines. Spain was building an Empire and needed the riches of the new world; its gold and silver and the crops of sugarcanes.

In the early days of the Spanish conquest, the local Indians were used as free labour. Later they were enslaved and forced to work by the Spanish. But the Indian population decreased rapidly, partly because of the wars, but also due to diseases brought by the Europeans, such as measles and the flu. In 1500, it is estimated that there were about 50 million Indians in the Americas. By 1600, this number had been reduced to about 8 million.

The Spanish authorities were alarmed at this decline in the local Indian population. New laws made by the Spanish in 1542 put an end to them being taken as slaves. Instead, a new system (the encomienda) was introduced according to which the Indians were obliged to do a certain amount of work for the Spanish landowner on whose land they lived, they were now serfs instead of slaves - though the difference was negligible.

To keep up the output of the mines or the plantations, the number of imported African slaves was increased. At first they were brought from other colonies owned by Spain, such as the Canary Islands in the Atlantic Ocean. Later, slaves were brought in greater numbers from West Africa.

The licence to sell slaves went to whomever was prepared to pay the most for it. Often this meant that Portuguese, Dutch, German, British, or Genoese merchants were supplying slaves to the Spanish colonies. From 1550 to 1595, the official records show that 36,300 enslaved Africans were imported into the Spanish-owned parts of South America. The number was probably much higher, as more were smuggled in by unlicensed slave traders.

In 1574, a census taken of the Greater Antilles reported 1000 Spaniards and 12,000 African slaves on Hispaniola.

1501年，首批非洲奴隶抵达伊斯帕尼奥拉岛，被送往矿井。西班牙正在建立帝国，需要新大陆的财富：黄金、白银和甘蔗作物。

西班牙征服初期，当地印第安人被当作免费劳力。后来，他们遭西班牙人奴役，被迫劳动。印第安人口迅速减少，部分原因是战争，也因为欧洲人带来的麻疹、流感等疾病。估计1500年美洲约有五千万印第安人；到1600年，这一数字已降至约八百万。

西班牙当局对当地印第安人口的锐减感到担忧。1542年，西班牙颁布新法，禁止再将印第安人抓去做奴隶。取而代之的是一种名为“恩贡米恩达制”（encomienda）的新制度：印第安人必须为其居住地所属的西班牙地主完成一定劳动；他们成了农奴而非奴隶——尽管两者差别微乎其微。

为了维持矿井和种植园的产量，输入非洲奴隶的数量随之增加。起初，他们来自西班牙拥有的其他殖民地，例如大西洋上的加那利群岛。后来，西非奴隶被大批运来。

奴隶贸易许可授予出价最高者。许多时候，这意味着由葡萄牙、荷兰、德国、英国或热那亚商人向西班牙殖民地供应奴隶。官方记录显示，1550年至1595年间，有36,300名被奴役的非洲人被运入西班牙在南美洲的领地。实际人数很可能更高，因为还有更多人被无证奴隶贩子走私入境。

1574年对大安的列斯群岛进行的人口普查报告称，伊斯帕尼奥拉岛有1,000名西班牙人和12,000名非洲奴隶。

Catedral de Santa María la Menor, aka. Cathedral of St. Mary of the Incarnation in Santo Domingo, is the oldest cathedral in the Americas. Consecrated by Pope Julius II in 1504, the construction of the Cathedral began in 1512 under the leadership of Bishop Fray García Padilla, was continued from 1519 by Bishop Alexander Geraldini, and lasted until 1540. The cathedral's very first stone was laid in 1502 by Christopher Columbus' son Diego Columbus. The construction was carried out by Luis Moya, according to plans designed by Alonso Rodriguez, of Seville, Spain. It was consecrated in 1541.

The walls of the cathedral are solid limestone. There are twelve side chapels, three aisles, and a nave. None of the side chapels were included in the original building, but have been added on later. The cathedral is fronted with a golden-tinted coral limestone façade, the church combines elements of both Gothic and Baroque with some lavish plateresque styles as exemplified by the high altar chiseled out of silver. There is also a treasury which has an excellent art collection of ancient woodcarvings, furnishings, funerary monuments, silver, and jewelry.

The remains of Christopher Columbus were once housed at the cathedral, before their final resting place in the Faro a Colon.

Catedral de Santa María la Menor does not have a bell tower. Because of lacking funds, it took the Spanish 29 years to build, and some features had to be omitted due to lack of money. The biggest toll the cathedral took was when British pirate Sir Francis Drake captured it and used it as his fortress. The damage sustained by the cathedral during the Drake's attacks and subsequent looting and plundering left many of the artifacts and artwork damaged beyond recovery. As a matter of fact, the cathedral's most valued artwork - the Madonna from the Chapel of the Virgin of Antigua - was stolen and spirited off to Spain in 1520. It was not returned back to the Dominican Republic until 1892.

圣玛丽亚·拉梅诺尔大教堂（Catedral de Santa María la Menor），又称圣多明各的圣玛丽亚（道成肉身）大教堂（Cathedral of St. Mary of the Incarnation），是美洲最古老的大教堂。教宗尤利乌斯二世于1504年为其祝圣；大教堂于1512年在加西亚·帕迪利亚修士主教主持下动工，1519年起由亚历山大·杰拉尔迪尼主教继续主持，直至1540年完工。大教堂的第一块基石由克里斯托弗·哥伦布之子迭戈·哥伦布于1502年铺设。工程由路易斯·莫亚承建，设计则出自西班牙塞维利亚的阿隆索·罗德里格斯。大教堂于1541年举行祝圣仪式。

大教堂的墙体由坚固的石灰岩砌成。内部有十二座侧礼拜堂、三条侧廊和一条中殿。所有侧礼拜堂都不在原始设计之中，而是后来增建的。大教堂正面采用金色调的珊瑚石灰岩；建筑融合了哥特式与巴洛克式元素，也展现出华丽的银匠式风格，例如用银雕琢而成的高坛。这里还有一座珍宝室，收藏着精美的古木雕、家具、墓葬纪念物、白银和珠宝。

克里斯托弗·哥伦布的遗骸曾安放在这座大教堂，后来才迁至最终安息之所——哥伦布灯塔。

圣玛丽亚·拉梅诺尔大教堂没有钟楼。由于资金短缺，西班牙人花了29年才将它建成，一些部分也因经费不足而省略。大教堂遭受的最大劫难，是英国海盗弗朗西斯·德雷克爵士攻占并将其用作堡垒。德雷克袭击后，大教堂遭到破坏，随后又被洗劫掠夺，许多文物和艺术品损毁严重，无法修复。事实上，大教堂最珍贵的艺术品——古安提瓜圣母礼拜堂中的圣母像——于1520年被盗并秘密运往西班牙，直到1892年才归还多米尼加共和国。

records_to_check.source:
Ozama is a Taino word that means wetlands or navigable waters. Fortaleza Ozama (Ozama Fortress) was built on the banks of the Ozama river, one of the most important rivers in the Dominican Republic. It springs in the North and runs 104 km (65 miles) until it reaches the Carribbean Ocean a few hundred meters from the Fortress.

The Fortaleza Ozama was constructed between 1502 and 1508 by order of the then Governor of Hispaniola, Fray Nicholas de Ovando, the founder of the city of Santo Domingo. It was built in order to defend the city against attacks by pirates and privateers. It has never been taken by force of arms.

One part of the Fortress is Torre del Homenaje or Tower of Homage. It was built in medieval style rising to a height of 18.5 meters (61 feet). It was built utilizing the labor of enslaved Tainos and Africans.

The tower is called Tower of Homage to glorify the Spanish conquistadors, who came there from Spain to conquer and colonise the newly discovered lands. It was from this fort in Old Santo Domingo that the famous expeditions of conquest began; Hernán Cortés in México, Diego Velásquez in Cuba, Francisco Pizarro in Perú, Alonso de Hojeda in Venezuela, Pazco Núñez Balboa in Panamá, and Ponce de León in Puerto Rico.

The tower was made of coral rock, which has the property of absorbing moisture, keeping the interior of the structure cool. No metals were used in the construction, and the cement - made of gypsum, clay, lime, and the blood of animals - becomes stronger with the passage of time.

Diego Colón, the son of Cristóbal Colón (Christopher Columbus) and his wife María de Toledo, temporarily lived in the Torre del Homenaje, occupying all of the second level, while their servants lived on the first level. The couple remained there for two years.

“奥萨马”是泰诺语，意为湿地或可通航的水域。奥萨马堡建在奥萨马河岸边；这条河是多米尼加共和国最重要的河流之一。它发源于北部，流经104公里（65英里），最终在距堡垒数百米处注入加勒比海。

奥萨马堡由伊斯帕尼奥拉岛时任总督弗雷·尼古拉斯·德·奥万多下令，于1502至1508年间修建；他也是圣多明各的建城者。修建这座堡垒是为了防御海盗和私掠船的袭击。它从未被武力攻陷。

堡垒的一部分是“致敬塔”（Torre del Homenaje）。这座中世纪风格的塔楼高18.5米（61英尺），由被奴役的泰诺人和非洲人劳作建成。

这座塔以“致敬”为名，旨在颂扬从西班牙远道而来、征服并殖民新发现土地的西班牙征服者。著名的征服远征正是从旧圣多明各的这座堡垒出发：埃尔南·科尔特斯前往墨西哥，迭戈·贝拉斯克斯前往古巴，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗前往秘鲁，阿隆索·德·奥赫达前往委内瑞拉，帕斯科·努涅斯·德·巴尔沃亚前往巴拿马，庞塞·德莱昂前往波多黎各。

塔楼由珊瑚岩建成，这种岩石能够吸收水分，使建筑内部保持凉爽。建造时没有使用金属；水泥由石膏、黏土、石灰和动物血制成，随着时间推移会愈发坚固。

克里斯托瓦尔·科隆（即克里斯托弗·哥伦布）之子迭戈·科隆曾暂住在致敬塔，占用了整整二层，仆人则住在一层。迭戈与妻子玛丽亚·德·托莱多在此住了两年。

The Masaya Volcanom, or the Masaya caldera, was formed 2500 years ago by a basaltic eruption of the Las Sierras shield volcano. The Masaya caldera covers 6 by 11.5 km and has all of 13 openings through which there is a constant emission of sulphur dioxide gas.

Masaya's last eruption of lava was in 1772. Since then, several minor explosions have occurred in addition to the emissions of gas.

The Masaya was feared both by the indigenous people and by the Spanish Conquistadors. It is told that the locals sought to appease the spirit of the volcano by sacrificing young girls, throwing them into the mouth of the volcano.

The Spanish Conquistadors at first thought the glistening lava was liquid gold, but as they experienced the heat and the poisonous fumes from the heart of the volcano, they named it "La Boca del Inferno" or "the Mouth of Hell". They also erected a cross on the edge of the crater and named it "La Cruz de Bobadilla" after Father Francisco Bobadilla, a Jesuit priest. By doing so, they hoped to exorcise the Devil.

马萨亚火山口（又称马萨亚破火山口）形成于约2500年前，是拉斯谢拉斯盾状火山的一次玄武岩喷发所致。马萨亚破火山口面积约为6×11.5公里，共有13个喷气口，持续排放二氧化硫。

马萨亚上一次熔岩喷发发生在1772年。此后除持续排气外，还发生过数次小规模爆发。

当地原住民和西班牙征服者都畏惧马萨亚。据说当地人曾将少女投入火山口献祭，以平息火山之灵。

西班牙征服者起初以为闪闪发亮的熔岩是液态黄金，但他们领教了火山深处的灼热与毒气后，便称它为“地狱之口”（La Boca del Inferno）。他们还在火山口边缘竖起十字架，以耶稣会神父弗朗西斯科·博巴迪利亚之名将其称为“博巴迪利亚十字架”（La Cruz de Bobadilla），希望借此驱逐恶魔。

当地原住民和西班牙征服者都畏惧马萨亚。据说当地人曾将少女投入火山口献祭，以平息火山之灵。

西班牙征服者起初以为闪闪发亮的熔岩是液态黄金，但他们领教了火山深处的灼热与毒气后，便称它为“地狱之口”（La Boca del Inferno）。他们还在火山口边缘竖起十字架，以耶稣会神父弗朗西斯科·博巴迪利亚之名将其称为“博巴迪利亚十字架”（La Cruz de Bobadilla），希望借此驱逐恶魔。

The Maya lived in three loosely defined zones: The Maya highlands, the Southern lowlands, and the Northern lowlands (all of the Yucatán peninsula). The height of the Maya empire was around 600 A.D. Their cities spread through Mesoamerica, and varied greatly depending on the topography. They evolved as nature dictated, even in the tropical rainforests.

The Maya excelled at agriculture, pottery, hieroglyph writing, calendar-making and mathematics, and left behind an astonishing amount of impressive architecture and symbolic artwork such as the stepped pyramids, similar to the architecture of the Toltec.

Most of the great stone cities of the Maya were abandoned by 900 A.D., and by the time of the Spanish conquest, the Maya were primarily living in small farming communities. Development persisted in the northern centers and the cities of the northern lowlands in Yucatán continued to flourish for centuries more; some of the important sites in this era were Chichen Itza, Uxmal, Edzná, and Coba. After the decline of the ruling dynasties of Chichen and Uxmal, Mayapan ruled all of Yucatán until a revolt in 1450. After this point, the area degenerated into competing city-states until Yucatán was conquered by the Spanish.

The Spanish conquest of Yucatan lasted 170 years. Unlike the Aztec and Inca Empires, there was no single Maya political center, therefore the conquistadors had to subdue the numerous independent Maya states (polities) one by one, many of which fought fiercely.

The Maya survived the Spanish colonization. The Maya and their descendants form sizable populations throughout the Maya area and maintain a distinctive set of traditions and beliefs. Millions of people still speak Maya languages.

玛雅人主要生活在三个界线并不分明的区域：玛雅高地、南部低地和北部低地（即整个尤卡坦半岛）。玛雅帝国的鼎盛时期约在公元600年。玛雅人的城市遍布中美洲，形态因地势而异；他们顺应自然环境发展，甚至在热带雨林中也如此。

玛雅人精于农业、制陶、象形文字书写、历法和数学，留下了数量惊人的宏伟建筑与象征性艺术品，例如阶梯金字塔；这类建筑与托尔特克人的风格相似。

到公元900年，大多数玛雅大型石城已被遗弃。西班牙征服时期，玛雅人主要生活在小型农耕社区。北部中心地区的发展仍在继续，尤卡坦北部低地的城市也繁荣了数百年；这一时期的重要遗址包括奇琴伊察、乌斯马尔、埃兹纳和科巴。奇琴伊察和乌斯马尔的统治王朝衰落后，玛雅潘统治了整个尤卡坦，直至1450年发生叛乱。此后当地分裂为相互竞争的城邦，最终被西班牙征服。

西班牙征服尤卡坦历时170年。与阿兹特克帝国和印加帝国不同，玛雅人没有单一的政治中心，因此征服者不得不逐一征服众多独立的玛雅政体，其中许多都进行了激烈抵抗。

玛雅人在西班牙殖民统治下延续至今。玛雅人及其后裔在玛雅地区广泛分布，并保有独特的传统与信仰。如今仍有数百万人讲玛雅语。

San Tiago de los Caballeros (Saint James of the Knights) also known as San Tiago de los 30 Caballeros, is the capital of Santiago Province. Whether founded in 1494 by Christopher Columbus (as some historians claim) or in 1495 by his brother Bartolomeo, San Tiago was among the first European settlements in America during the first wave of European colonization of the New World.

It is situated on the Yaque del Norte River, in the heart of the fertile Cibao Valley.

The original colony was in the city of Jacagua. In 1504, 30 caballeros of the Order of St. James (San Tiago) moved from nearby La Isabela to San Tiago,  and from that time the city was known as San Tiago de los Caballeros.

When the knights returned back to Spain they put a formal complaint before the king stating that their horses had been unfairly commissioned as beasts of burden and their weapons had been appropriated by Diego and Bartolome Columbus and that they had been made to do manual labor, something considered beneath their station as knights, who were meant to engage only in battle. The king compensated them for all their losses.

After being destroyed by an earthquake in 1562, the city was rebuilt a few miles away, where Nibaje Stream meets the Yaque; ruins of the old city are still visible in the district of San Francisco de Jacagua. San Tiago survived numerous earthquakes and fires to serve repeatedly as the republic's capital.

圣地亚哥-德洛斯卡瓦列罗斯（San Tiago de los Caballeros），又称“三十骑士圣地亚哥”，是圣地亚哥省的首府。部分历史学家认为它由克里斯托弗·哥伦布于1494年建立，另一些人则认为是其兄弟巴托洛梅奥于1495年建立；无论如何，它都是新大陆第一波欧洲殖民浪潮中最早的一批欧洲人定居点之一。

这座城市坐落在亚克德尔诺特河畔，位于肥沃的西包谷地中心。

最初的殖民地位于哈卡瓜城。1504年，圣雅各骑士团的30名骑士从附近的拉伊莎贝拉迁至圣地亚哥，此后这座城市便被称为“圣地亚哥-德洛斯卡瓦列罗斯”。

骑士们返回西班牙后，正式向国王申诉：迭戈和巴托洛梅奥·哥伦布不公地征用了他们的马匹作为驮兽、夺走了他们的武器，还逼他们从事体力劳动。这些工作有失骑士身份；骑士本应只投身战斗。国王补偿了他们的一切损失。

1562年地震摧毁了这座城市，之后它在数英里外、尼巴赫溪与亚克河交汇处重建。旧城遗址至今仍可在圣弗朗西斯科-德哈卡瓜区看到。圣地亚哥历经多次地震与火灾，曾多次成为共和国首都。

In the 9th and 10th centuries, several groups of migrants came from the North and South to the Mesoamerican plains/The Mexican Basin. One of the first groups was the Toltecs, supposed to be escapees from the fall of Teotihuacán. The Toltecs founded the city of Tula or Tollan, which became the dominant city in Mesoamerica 900-1100, although it never reached the same size as Teotihuacán due to competing cities in the area.

The Toltec culture disappeared in the 12th century, possibly overrun by the Chichimecas. The Chichimecas' culture slowly disappeared, and central Mexico entered a chaotic dark age until the Aztecs rose to power in Tenochtitlán at what is now Mexico City, in the early 1300s.

The Aztecs respected the Toltecs as "men of knowledge", and rewrote some of their own history to show they were related to the Toltecs. The word Toltec is said to come from the Nahuatl language of that area, and means "master builder" or "artist".
 
There are no written records left by the Toltec. What we know about them is what we see in the ruins they left behind, and what later Mesoamerican people have written. We don't know what language they spoke, but it is supposed to have been some form of Nahuatl.

We also don't know whether the Toltec civilization was an empire in its own right (some call it the third of the great empires in the Basin of Mexico) or whether it was a mythical and philosophical construct by the Aztecs or other Mesoamericans that was used to symbolize the might and sophistication of several different civilizations. However, traces of their culture can be found even among the Mayans in Chichén Itza, 1500 km from Tula and in the Northamerican Southwest.

9至10世纪，来自南北的多个移民群体来到中美洲平原/墨西哥盆地。其中最早的一支是托尔特克人，据说他们是从特奥蒂瓦坎陷落后逃出的难民。托尔特克人建立了图拉城（又称托兰），该城于900至1100年间成为中美洲的主导城市；但由于周边城市竞争，它始终不及特奥蒂瓦坎规模宏大。

托尔特克文化在12世纪消失，可能是被奇奇梅克人征服。奇奇梅克文化也逐渐消亡，墨西哥中部随之进入混乱的黑暗时期，直到14世纪初阿兹特克人在如今墨西哥城所在地的特诺奇蒂特兰崛起。

阿兹特克人尊崇托尔特克人为“知识之民”，还改写了部分自身历史，以显示他们与托尔特克人的渊源。据说“托尔特克”一词来自当地的纳瓦特尔语，意为“大师级建造者”或“艺术家”。

托尔特克人没有留下任何文字记录。我们对他们的了解来自他们留下的遗迹，以及后来的中美洲人所写的记载。我们不知道他们说什么语言，但据说那是纳瓦特尔语的一种形式。

我们同样不知道托尔特克文明是否是一个独立帝国（有人称其为墨西哥盆地三大帝国中的第三个），还是阿兹特克人或其他中美洲人构想出的神话与哲学体系，用来象征多个文明的力量与高度发展。不过，即使在距图拉1500公里的奇琴伊察玛雅遗址，以及北美西南部，也能发现托尔特克文化的痕迹。

examples.source: "Uncle Miguel taught me - well he's not my real uncle but he might as well be family - but he left a few months ago because he thought it was dangerous to stay in Xalapa. He came with Capitán Gutiérrez but stayed behind when his expedition left because he liked it here and-- and he taught me lots of things about Spain and Europe and to understand and speak Spanish so I could translate for father."
examples.translation: “米格尔叔叔教我的——好吧，他不是我亲叔叔，但也算是家人了——可几个月前他就离开了，因为他觉得留在哈拉帕很危险。他跟着队长古铁雷斯一起来的，但远征队离开时他留了下来，因为他喜欢这里，而且——而且他教了我很多关于西班牙和欧洲的事，还教我听懂和说西班牙语，这样我就能替父亲翻译了。”

examples.source: "Your /father's/ property? I have every right. I could turn the cannons of the fortress on your ship and send it to the bottom of the Ozama River if I decided to, and you would have no recourse to stop me. The sooner you realise that your objections are futile, the sooner we can get down to the business of how you might earn my permission to mount your expedition, hmm?"
examples.translation: “你/父亲的/财产？我有这个权利。只要我愿意，大可用堡垒的火炮轰击你的船只，把它送进奥萨马河底；你也无权阻止我。你越早明白你的反对毫无用处，我们就越早能谈谈你要怎样才能赢得我准许你组织远征，嗯？”

examples.source:
"Un sobrynn' est' abadessa avi', a que mui gran ben 
queria, que era men' e apost' e fremoso. 
Este, des que viu a monja, quis-lle mellor d'outra ren, 
e en guisar que a ouvesse foi tan aguçoso, que non era dia 
que ll' el muitas vegadas sa coita non dizia e lle prometia 
que sse con el sse fosse, con ela casaria."
examples.translation:
“修女院长有个侄儿，她很疼爱他；
他年轻、端庄又俊美。
他一见那修女，便觉得她胜过世间一切；
为了得到她，他费尽心思，十分急切，
日日多次向她倾诉自己的苦恋，还许诺说：
只要她跟他走，他就娶她为妻。”

examples.source: "I can't stand that we allow FName2, that filthy savage, to sleep in our camp. If we /absolutely must/ suffer FHimHer2 to follow us around like some mangy stray dog, so be it - but at the very least you could make FHimHer2 sleep outside the camp."
examples.translation: “我受不了我们竟让FName2——那个肮脏的野蛮人——睡在营地里。要是我们/确实非得/忍受FHimHer2像条浑身癞病的流浪狗似的跟着我们，那也罢；但至少，你可以让FHimHer2睡在营地外。”

examples.source: "You /animals!/ You sons of bitches! Disgusting savages! Filthy cowards! We had an understanding, FHeShe1 was not to be harmed before the sacrifice! You kill a FManWoman1, fine - but you get it over with! Look at this poor FBoyGirl1! Look what you've /done/ to FHimHer1!"
examples.translation: “你们这群/畜生！/你们这群狗娘养的！令人作呕的野蛮人！肮脏的懦夫！我们说好了，献祭之前不许伤害FHeShe1！杀一个FManWoman1也行——但至少给个痛快！看看这个可怜的FBoyGirl1！看看你们对FHimHer1/做/了什么！”

examples.source: "Capitán PNameLast. An idea, if I may. The savages are tricky, we don't know what kind of traps they've laid for us down there. I suggest we enter the temple calmly, pretending we have no hostile intentions."
examples.translation: “队长PNameLast，恕我直言，我有个主意。这些野蛮人狡猾得很，我们不知道他们在下面布置了什么陷阱。我建议我们平静地进入神殿，假装没有敌意。”

examples.source: "FNameFirst2 has a very strong fever, but I'm not seeing any other symptoms yet. It's some sort of disease, I can't tell which - could just be a cold, but either way it seems FHeShe2 will be out of commission for a while. Have the servants clear a place for FNameFirst2 on the carts, if you will."
examples.translation: “FNameFirst2发高烧了，不过目前还没发现其他症状。应该是某种疾病，我说不准是哪一种——也可能只是感冒；但无论如何，看来FHeShe2得休养一阵子。劳烦你让仆人在马车上给FNameFirst2腾个位置。”

examples.source: "I'm not doing this to get to you, /PNameFirst/. These are all the people I have left after you murdered my troops in that God damned ravine, when that self-obsessed /bastardo/ Leandra betrayed me and fell in my back. I need to curry favour with the Taíno, and FNameFirst1 here is my ballast."
examples.translation: “我这么做不是为了针对你，/PNameFirst/。你在那该死的峡谷里杀了我的部下；那个自以为是的/混蛋/莱安德拉又背叛我，从背后捅了我一刀。如今我只剩下这些人。我得讨好泰诺人，而FNameFirst1就是我的筹码。”

examples.source: "My wife was doing a fine enough job of raising and protecting my sons. I had not been there for them until then, and they did not seem to be worse off for suffering my absence. No, mi PSenorSenora: I do not belong in Spain - not any longer."
examples.translation: “我妻子把儿子们照顾得很好，也保护得很好。在那之前，我从未陪伴过他们；而他们似乎并没有因为我的缺席而过得更糟。不，PSenorSenora：我不属于西班牙——至少如今不属于了。”

examples.source: "Eh, my father wasn't a military man. I want to fight the rebels. I don't know if they even understand, but they're tearing Hispaniola apart. I thought I could fight the rebels with Noriega, but he's terrified to send his troops out of Santo Domingo anymore."
examples.translation: “嗯，我父亲不是军人。我想和叛军作战。我不知道他们是否明白，可他们正在把伊斯帕尼奥拉岛撕得四分五裂。我原以为可以和诺列加一起对付叛军，可他对派兵一事心怀恐惧，再也不敢派部队离开圣多明各了。”

examples.translation: “没错，但这些不会成为回忆录。我一直很热衷于钻研——嗯……虚构作品。古希腊史诗给了我/如此/多的灵感。我希望有朝一日能把自己的故事添进那些传奇作品之中，让它们也能在家乡那座宏伟图书馆里与之并列。”

The name Xipe Totec means "Our Lord the Flayed One", and he was usually depicted as a flayed man clad in his own skin.

He was the Aztec god of agriculture, spring, and seasons, and the symbol of the death and rebirth of nature. Xipe Totec was also the god of the east and the patron of gold smiths.

He was called the flayed god, because according to myth, he flayed himself to stimulate growth in both nature and man. When he had shed his skin, he would reappear as a shining, golden god.

Each year in the beginning of spring, he was honoured by human sacrifices. The priests removed the hearts from the victims while they were still alive, then the priests flayed the bodies and put on the skins, which had been coloured yellow. The yellow skins were called teocuitlaquemitl (golden clothes). Other victims were fastened to a frame and killed with arrows. The blood dripping from these sacrifizes symbolised the fertile spring rain. These rituals symbolized the renewal of the earth and the budding of new life.

Xipe Totec was also known by the names Tlatlauhca, Tlatlauhqui Tezcatlipoca ("Red Smoking Mirror") and Youalahuan ("the Night Drinker").

Xipe Totec

The name Xipe Totec means "Our Lord the Flayed One", and he was usually depicted as a flayed man clad in his own skin.

He was the Aztec god of agriculture, spring, and seasons, and the symbol of the death and rebirth of nature. Xipe Totec was also the god of the east and the patron of gold smiths.

He was called the flayed god, because according to myth, he flayed himself to stimulate growth in both nature and man. When he had shed his skin, he would reappear as a shining, golden god.

Each year in the beginning of spring, he was honoured by human sacrifices. The priests removed the hearts from the victims while they were still alive, then the priests flayed the bodies and put on the skins, which had been coloured yellow. The yellow skins were called teocuitlaquemitl (golden clothes). Other victims were fastened to a frame and killed with arrows. The blood dripping from these sacrifizes symbolised the fertile spring rain. These rituals symbolized the renewal of the earth and the budding of new life.

Xipe Totec was also known by the names Tlatlauhca, Tlatlauhqui Tezcatlipoca ("Red Smoking Mirror") and Youalahuan ("the Night Drinker").

Masaya Volcano

The Masaya Volcanom, or the Masaya caldera, was formed 2500 years ago by a basaltic eruption of the Las Sierras shield volcano. The Masaya caldera covers 6 by 11.5 km and has all of 13 openings through which there is a constant emission of sulphur dioxide gas.

Masaya's last eruption of lava was in 1772. Since then, several minor explosions have occurred in addition to the emissions of gas.

The Masaya was feared both by the indigenous people and by the Spanish Conquistadors. It is told that the locals sought to appease the spirit of the volcano by sacrificing young girls, throwing them into the mouth of the volcano.

The Spanish Conquistadors at first thought the glistening lava was liquid gold, but as they experienced the heat and the poisonous fumes from the heart of the volcano, they named it "La Boca del Inferno" or "the Mouth of Hell". They also erected a cross on the edge of the crater and named it "La Cruz de Bobadilla" after Father Francisco Bobadilla, a Jesuit priest. By doing so, they hoped to exorcise the Devil.

evidence.text:
Xolotl was known as The Twin or The Lord of the West, and was the god of fire and bad luck. He was Quetzalcoatl's twin, sons of the virgin Coatlicue, and Quetzalcoatl's double. He was the dark personification of Venus, the evening star, and he guarded the sun on its journey through the underworld at night.

He was a dog-like deity, often depicted with ragged ears, and was identified with sickness and physical deformity. He was also sometimes depicted as a skeleton or a man with the head of a dog (dogs were considered filthy and immoral in the Mesoamerican cultures, and likewise, twins were considered a type of deformity).

According to myth, he accompanied Quetzalcoatl to Mictlan, the land of death, to retrieve the bones from those who inhabited the previous world (Nahui Atl) in order to create new life for this world (Nahui Olin), and he assisted Quetzalcoatl in bringing humankind and fire from the underworld.

In another creation myth it was Xolotl who brought a bone to the gods, who sprinkled it with some of their blood and transformed it into a boy and a girl: the first of the human race.
